newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: HOWARD FAILS TO TAKE RACE DEBATE FURTHER
The Prime Minister hasn't taken up the challenge from the Anglican Bishop of Canberra to state his views on racism more clearly.
At a religious service in Parliament House last night attended by 500 people, Bishop George Browning called on Mr Howard to express unambiguously where he stands on a multicultural, tolerant society.
Mr Howard gave a short welcoming address to a prayer breakfast in Parliament House this morning, but didn't take up Bishop Browning's challenge to speak out again on racism.
JOINT STATE WORKING PARTY ON TRADE
The Northern Territory and Tasmanian governments will set up a working party to look at ways of increasing trade links between the two regions.
Tasmanian Premier Tony Rundle is in the Top End, on a fact-finding trip, at the invitatiion of Chief Minister Shane Stone.
Mr Rundle says the potential for co-operation between the two regions is good, with Tasmania having agricultural markets in North Asia and the Territory having markets in Southeast Asia.
The New South Wales Government is under fire for seemingly failing to protect the state's koala population.
The Opposition says the government has failed to implement measures to protect koalas - despite introducing them under planning regulations more than a year ago.
Shadow environment Minister Brad Hazzard, says councils are urgently seeking guidelines on how to manage koala populations.
CALLS FOR BETTER DEAL FOR ISOLATED CHILDREN
A group of parents from remote rural Australia is seeking better access to education for their children.
The National Council of the Isolated Children's Parents Association says remote students are the least educated socio-economic group in the country with only half completing Year 12.

The Council is in Canberra where it will meet with politicians including Education Minister Amanda Vanstone and Social Securities Minister Jocelyn Newmann to appeal for increased funding of education assistance schemes.
President Jenny McLellan says some geographically isolated familes are forced to move to provide their children with an education.
